title: Observability: provider-layer logs missing algo name for shared callbacks
description: wolfssl_sha_update, wolfssl_sha_finalize, wolfssl_sha_sess_reset (wolfssl_sha.c), wolfssl_hmac_update, wolfssl_hmac_finalize, wolfssl_hmac_sess_reset (wolfssl_hmac.c), and wolfssl_cmac_aes_sess_reset (wolfssl_cmac.c) are shared callbacks used by multiple algo variants. Their pr_err_ratelimited lines log only __func__ and the raw wc_err — there is no algo name. When one of these fires, a support engineer cannot tell from the ring buffer whether the failure was in sha256 vs sha512, or hmac(sha256) vs hmac(sha512), without attaching a debugger to inspect ctx->type or ctx->hash_type. The ctx struct carries that information; it just is not included in the log message. Affected lines: wolfssl_sha.c:139 (sha_sess_init), :309 (wolfssl_sha_update), :367 (wolfssl_sha_finalize); wolfssl_hmac.c:128 (hmac_sess_init), :269 (wolfssl_hmac_update), :311 (wolfssl_hmac_finalize); wolfssl_cmac.c:133 (wolfssl_cmac_aes_sess_reset).
close_reason: Fixed: xlat pr_debug→pr_err, sha/hmac algo-name helpers, lookup_algo provider_name_out
